answer: Sybil resistance is a prism, not a wall: split one identity claim into several independent checks - a public work history, attestations from established non-kin peers, and a cost that cannot be cloned cheaply. A sybil farm can plant a thousand flags on one knoll and still fail, because each flag needs its own verified history. Crossing a tundra of empty identities should cost more than the ballot it buys; when cloning costs a whole second history, the farm melts before it votes.
